text:
alex: hey — quick help? staging terraform plan stuck after a manual import. it just sits at 'Refreshing state...' for >10m after we ran the import. we imported a k8s serviceaccount. anyone seen this?
chloe: did you check the backend lock? if there's a DynamoDB lock the plan will wait. run `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name redwood-tf-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S": "..."}}'` or `terraform force-unlock LOCKID`
sam: also check if the import changed the resource address. run `terraform state list | grep service_account` to see duplicates.
maria: is it tainted? `terraform untaint <addr>` or if the import didn't wire correctly `terraform state rm` + `terraform import` can help. which provider are you using for the SA?
alex: provider is kubernetes v2.5.2. output when it hangs: 
```
Refreshing state... [id=module.k8s.kube_service_account.default]
2026/03/18 15:12:05 [DEBUG] plugin: waiting for lock release
```
also here's our backend config: 
```hcl
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket         = "redwood-terraform-staging"
    key            = "clusters/staging/terraform.tfstate"
    region         = "us-west-2"
    dynamodb_table = "redwood-tf-locks"
  }
}
```
chloe: if the lock is stale and no one's running, `terraform force-unlock LOCKID` is fine but double-check the lock metadata (owner, start time).
sam: you can try `terraform plan -refresh=false` to bypass the refresh step and see the planned diffs. also `TF_LOG=TRACE terraform plan` gives more detail on where it hangs.
maria: if the import used a different ID format, TF can think there are two resources. I fixed a similar case with: `terraform state rm module.k8s.kube_service_account.default` then `terraform import module.k8s.kube_service_account.default kube-system:sa/myname` — landed cleanly.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: CI job #4825 (infra/staging) finished — no active terraform runs reported.
alex: thanks — found a stale lock entry `lock-20260318-5f2b` in dynamodb, forced unlock, re-ran plan. it progressed to show: `Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy` but it's proposing to recreate the SA because annotations differ (Argo rewrites them). will try untaint/import again or coordinate with platform to pause Argo. :thumbsup:
chloe: if annotations are the only drift consider `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }` on the k8s manifest so Argo vs TF don't fight.
sam: and check whether the controller re-applies a timestamp/managed-by annotation — that'll force recreate every run. if so, coordinate with platform team.
alex: yep Argo was reconciling. i'll pause the app sync, untaint + import, then plan/apply. will post results. thanks for the quick help.
maria: nice — ping us if it goes weird, we can jump in for an apply window.
